rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
Ritual / practice (noun) / ceremony — hard ban
No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lines 1-36 maintain AE101 voice quintet register: Boris-precise (factual claims about gates), Rory reframe (green is a claim, not proof), maintained skepticism tone without reassurance. Explicitly named in maintainer as target.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Rough-cut drafts for articles.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, not an article draft.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 19: Goodhart's law named and bolded. Line 31-32: W. Edwards Deming credited by name for tampering concept. Line 14: Hamel Husain credited inline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses no third-person student references. Pronoun references to agent and gate, never to student-as-observer.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms used in body (gate, judge, verifier, passing, claim) are all earned through context and teaching of the lecture itself. No maintainer-specific vocabulary leaks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body maintains direct, factual tone. No reassurance-shaped softening (no 'no penalty', 'fine way to', 'it's OK if'). Consistent with Boris-precise register and designed doubt-opening stance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture format does not include a reference artifact with 'Frame to land' section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: One practitioner name in body: Hamel Husain (line 14). W. Edwards Deming named but in context of cultural-vocabulary attribution (tampering principle), not as primary module practitioner.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Title 'The gate is a claim too' and opening line establish punchy framing. Body sections explore five ways gates lie, providing depth and nuance downstream. Carve-out implicit in the teaching arc.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body contains no defensive positioning language ('not aspirational', 'not vendor', 'unlike consultancy', 'grounded in actual'). Teaching focused on principles and practice, not positioning.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: By M5, terms like 'gate', 'judge', 'verifier' have been established. 'Goodhart's law' and 'tampering' are named principles, not pre-planted jargon. Vocabulary appropriate for module position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No fenced prompts in body. Rule applies to exercises with trimmed forcing functions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Past tense for exercise recap sections — heading and body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, not an exercise. No 'What happened:' recap section present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses peer-flat language when describing systems and behavior. No combative verbs (bark, order, command, whip, drag, boss) directed at agent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All five section headers are literally true: 'Passing is not proof' (results from unknown cause), 'Judge needs calibrating' (accuracy unknown without measurement), 'Gates decay' (measures become targets), 'One run is a sample' (behavior is distribution), 'Change on recurrence' (statistical principle).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body does not frame student as lacking or correctable. Teaches principles without gap-focused framing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Terms 'gate', 'judge', 'verifier' are used in earned context. 'Passing' and 'claim' are common English. Technical concepts explained within their sections.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Business-audience word ban (Agents 101 default).
rules_evaluated.evidence: No business jargon (substrate, leverage, synergize, paradigm shift) in body. Direct, technical register maintained.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body does not conflate memory and context. No misuse of these curriculum terms.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No troubleshooting branches or recovery steps in body. Focused teaching path.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, not an exercise with prompts. Rule applies to exercise structures.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, not an exercise with debrief. Rule applies to module compounds.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle another module's voice.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintains consistent AE101 M5 voice (Boris-Rory, gate-skepticism) throughout. No tone shifts from other modules.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture does not ask students to manually diff or spot-check output. No student moves described.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Simulation personas never alone.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is not a simulation. Rule applies to simulations only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body contains no callout boxes labeled 'What research says'. Uses inline citations instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture describes no student moves. No prompts or actions described.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Specify which CLAUDE.md layer — every time.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body makes no reference to CLAUDE.md layers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses no em-dashes (—) or —. Hyphens used for list markers only. Sentences are simple and direct.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture uses declarative headers for understanding (appropriate for teaching mode, not exercise mode). Headers are literally true about mechanisms they describe, matching lecture rather than exercise register.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body contains no links to other curriculum surfaces.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first student-authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture does not ask students to author artifacts. No contested words introduced for authoring.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 19: 'agent' used appropriately for actor/optimizer. No conflation of LLM thinking with agent acting. Vocabulary matches context and M5 sophistication level.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body contains no time-of-day references (tomorrow, overnight, tonight, etc.). Module-relative phrasing not needed in lecture.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body does not announce reflection moments. No explicit contemplative-pause headers or prefixes. Principles stand on their own.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No meta-ask when student has already decided.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture contains no prompts. Rule applies to exercises with Claude interactions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: `.md` is default file type for student artifacts across curriculum.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture does not ask students to save artifacts. Rule applies to exercise prompts.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Each section teaches one principle and its countermove. No implementation details or administrative asides. Information density appropriate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body "read it" / "look at it" / "notice X" after chat-print = dead weight.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture does not describe chat-printed artifacts. No reading instructions after outputs.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture does not contain forward-looking asides with closers. Closing line addresses systemic principle, not student as subject.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture does not establish operational settings. Rule applies to exercises with repeating setup.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture body contains no fenced prompts with student copy-this affordance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompt blocks in lecture body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No prompts in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood 'gate-skepticism after the build' (named in maintainer, line 41) is honored throughout body. Opens doubt about gate reliability, maintains skepticism, does not resolve to optimism. Appropriate M5 closer mood.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Epistemic mood ≠ punitive mood.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mood is about uncertainty and unknowing (epistemic), not about student blame or failure. Skepticism about gate reliability, not about student performance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Title and sections lead with positive disciplines (building gates, calibrating judges, understanding distributions, measuring recurrence) not with failure words. Failure modes appear as context for countermoves, not as frame.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Lecture is M5 closer (confirmed in maintainer line 43). Does not front-run downstream M6 teaching moments. Maintains focus on gate principles without pre-teaching M6 work.
